prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1411; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle was stopped at a red light when struck from behind by a third-party vehicle. Police report requested. Claimant reports neck and right wrist pain and was transported to urgent care by ambulance from the scene.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant by phone. Claimant confirmed she is not represented by an attorney and wishes to handle the claim directly. Advised claimant of the right to seek counsel and of the bodily injury claim process. Claimant provided urgent care discharge paperwork showing X-ray findings consistent with a wrist fracture. Requested full medical records and authorization to obtain them.

Entry 3: Received signed medical authorization from claimant. Orthopedic referral noted in urgent care notes; follow-up appointment confirmed for the claimant. Claimant reports she is unable to work at her current position while in a cast and has asked about wage loss documentation. Sent employer verification form and explained the process for submitting pay stubs.

Entry 4: Reviewed photos submitted by the insured showing rear bumper damage to the claimant's vehicle and front-end damage to the at-fault vehicle. Appraisal assigned for both vehicles. Liability appears clear based on the police report narrative and the statement from the at-fault driver, who acknowledged the vehicle did not stop in time.

Entry 5: Claimant called to check status. Explained that the bodily injury evaluation will wait until orthopedic treatment is complete and the prognosis is documented. Reminded claimant she may request an itemized statement of medical bills at any time. Diary set to follow up in thirty days or upon receipt of orthopedic records, whichever comes first.
